analysis.evidence: יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהִים is the subject, עַל הָאָדָם identifies the man as the recipient, and לֵאמֹר introduces the words of the command.
analysis.morphology: Piel wayyiqtol, third masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־ and an apocopated verb form.

analysis.evidence: יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהִים is the subject of וַיְצַו (‘he commanded’). יַהְוֶה names the one who gives the command, and אֱלֹהִים (‘God’) stands in apposition to the name.
analysis.morphology: Proper noun, masculine singular, without prefix or suffix
analysis.sense: Personal name of the God of Israel

analysis.evidence: אֱלֹהִים stands in apposition to יַהְוֶה. Together they name the single subject of וַיְצַו, “he commanded,” the masculine singular verb introducing the command to the man.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine plural, absolute, with singular reference.

analysis.evidence: In וַיְצַו יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהִים עַל הָאָדָם, עַל marks the man as the one upon whom God lays the command. לֵאמֹר introduces the words addressed to him.
analysis.sense: upon, as a burden or responsibility

analysis.evidence: In וַיְצַו יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהִים עַל הָאָדָם, the definite article identifies the man already introduced in the garden narrative as the recipient of the command. The second-person masculine singular תֹּאכֵל addresses him directly.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ + masculine singular common noun in the absolute state.

analysis.evidence: לֵאמֹר introduces the words of the command reported by וַיְצַו. The second-person verb תֹּאכֵל shows that God addresses the man directly.
analysis.morphology: Qal infinitive construct with prefixed preposition לְ.

analysis.evidence: In מִכֹּל עֵץ הַגָּן, כֹּל quantifies the singular עֵץ. The permission אָכֹל תֹּאכֵל thus applies to any tree of the garden.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun with prefixed מִן, whose נ assimilates to the following כ.

analysis.evidence: עֵץ is in construct with הַגָּן, “the garden.” The phrase מִכֹּל עֵץ הַגָּן means “from every tree of the garden” and identifies the trees from which the man may eat.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular construct, without prefix or suffix

analysis.evidence: In מִכֹּל עֵץ הַגָּן, “from every tree of the garden,” הַגָּן completes the construct phrase עֵץ הַגָּן and identifies the garden to which the trees belong.
analysis.morphology: Singular absolute noun with the prefixed definite article הַ־.

analysis.evidence: In אָכֹל תֹּאכֵל, the infinitive absolute precedes a finite verb of the same root and emphasizes the permission to eat from any tree of the garden.
analysis.morphology: Qal infinitive absolute, without prefix or suffix

analysis.evidence: God addresses הָאָדָם directly. The preceding infinitive absolute אָכֹל emphasizes the permission expressed by תֹּאכֵל, yielding “you may freely eat.” מִכֹּל עֵץ הַגָּן identifies the trees from which he may eat.
analysis.morphology: Qal imperfect, second person masculine singular, with the person prefix ת־ and no suffix.
